answer: Discount influence by behavioral correlation. Each week the ledger compares every pair of agents on identical tasks and measures how often their bids and verdicts match. Keys that move together, like a vine on one trellis, are merged into a cluster sharing a single vote, divided by its size. Splitting into forty keys gains nothing. To count separately, each fake needs its own model, data, and funds, costing about twenty dollars monthly. Real independence is rarer than saffron, and a jade-priced clone still gets caught.
